HFpEF is included because exertional dyspnea out of proportion to cough is common in older or hypertensive/diabetic patients, and pulmonary congestion can cause chronic cough (‘cardiac cough’); however, absence of orthopnea, edema, or known cardiac risk factors reduces confidence. Sarcoidosis is considered due to granulomatous lung involvement causing cough and dyspnea, but its multisystem features (e.g., uveitis, erythema nodosum) are absent in this limited history, making it lower-confidence.
